posts.title: What we ask on the first call
posts.excerpt: The planning call is mostly questions: mornings, timing, budget and documents. Here is what we ask and why.
posts.content:
Every trip we plan begins with a forty-five-minute video call, and the call is mostly questions. Before we talk about places, we want to know how the two of you like to spend a morning, how far you are happy to walk, and what a good evening looks like.

We ask about timing next: the month you can go, how many nights you can spare, and whether the date is fixed by a wedding, an anniversary or a school holiday. Honeymoons usually start four to nine months ahead, while an anniversary weekend can be planned in six weeks.

Then comes the budget. We prefer to hear a range for the whole trip, flights included, because most honeymoons we plan cost between €6,000 and €14,000 for two. Our own planning fee is separate and fixed, and we take no commission from hotels, so nothing in the route is there for our benefit.

Last, we ask about documents: passports, visas, a name change after the wedding. Priya checks every entry rule twice. After the call you receive a first route and a fee within seven days, and you can change it twice before anything is booked.
